text:
alex: Customer reported intermittent truncation of tool-call args during streaming (SSE). Schema validation fails because the JSON payload ends mid-object. Sample tail: '...\"params\":{\"query\":\"find users by email\",\"limit\":10' and then connection continues but the JSON is incomplete. Happening more under high throughput routes.

 tori: Can you paste the raw SSE capture (raw chunk boundaries)? Also which client and what sits in front of Redwood (ALB/nginx/other)?

 alex: Pasting redacted capture from customer (raw):

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

1a\r\ndata: {"id":101,"tool":"search","params":{"query":"find users by email","limit":10}\r\n

13\r\ndata: {"id":102,"tool":"lookup","params":{"email":"user@example.com","meta":{\n

5\r\n```

Notice the second event ends mid-json. When parsed, the tool-call handler throws schema error.


 mike: Looks like chunk boundary splits the JSON mid-byte. Could be upstream proxy buffering or chunked-encoding mismatch. Does the ALB/nginx modify or gzip the stream?


 alex: Topology: customer function -> API Gateway -> ALB -> nginx proxy -> Redwood edge. Headers: Transfer-Encoding: chunked, Content-Type: text/event-stream, Gzip: sometimes on by default. Heartbeats: they use keepalive pings every 15s.


 eng-runtime: Hypothesis: an intermediate is buffering/flushing at newline or size limits, splitting multi-byte sequences, or closing the connection on client reconnect which leaves a partial event. Also gzip and re-chunking can corrupt event boundaries. We need a raw TCP capture across the ALB/nginx boundary.


 alex: here's a trimmed tcp view they provided (hex/CRLFs):

```
0000: 0d 0a 31 33 0d 0a 64 61 74 61 3a 20 7b 22 69 64 22\r\n0001: 00 3a 31 30 32 2c 22 74 6f 6f 6c 22 3a 22 6c\r\n0002: 6f 6f 6b 75 70 22 2c 22 70 61 72 61 6d 73 22 3a 7b\r\n0003: 22 65 6d 61 69 6c 22 3a 22 75 73 65 72 40 65 78 61\r\n0004: 6d 70 6c 65 2e 63 6f 6d 22 2c 22 6d 65 74 61 22 3a\r\n0005: 7b 0d 0a\r\n```
Ends right after a CRLF inside an inner object. Looks like a flush happened during UTF-8 sequence for some accented names too in other captures.


 tori: If the ALB/nginx are re-chunking, the chunk-size hex should reflect the true byte length. But some proxies apply buffering and then emit smaller chunks. Try disabling gzip and any buffering (nginx: proxy_buffering off, add header X-Accel-Buffering: no). Also ensure proxy_http_version 1.1 and set Connection: keep-alive.


 mike: For a reproducible test:
1) curl -N --http1.1 to the SSE endpoint to see raw streaming locally.
2) Repeat test with ALB in front and capture tcpdump at the edge.
3) Force payloads with multi-byte chars and a few kilobytes to force chunk boundaries.

If the issue only appears with ALB in front, likely the ALB/windowing behavior is the cause.


 alex: Customer ran step 1 (direct to Redwood) — no truncation. Step 2 (via ALB) — truncation shows up ~1/50 requests. Turning off gzip reduced rate by ~70%. They also observed fewer failures when keepalive_timeout set higher.


 eng-runtime: Two mitigation ideas:
- Short-term: server-side tolerance: delay schema validation for a short window (e.g., 1.5–2s) while tracking 'more data' signals to allow reassembly of fragmented events. Also: soft-fail with 4xx instead of 5xx to avoid noisy upstream retries.
- Medium-term: add an optional end-sentinel for tool args in the streaming protocol (e.g., append a base64 checksum or newline sentinel) so partial fragments can be detected and re-requested/reassembled.


 support-bot: Ticket #12345 updated: escalated to eng-runtime.


 alex: Action items — ask infra/customer to: disable gzip, set X-Accel-Buffering: no (or equivalent), ensure proxy_http_version 1.1, and capture raw tcp at ALB/nginx boundary. Eng-runtime to add a metric for "toolcall_partial_json" and consider a short wait-before-validate heuristic.


 tori: I'll take ownership of follow-up with eng-runtime. Can we also add a small log hook that captures the last 4KB of the stream (redacting PII) when a parse error occurs? That will speed diagnostics.


 eng-runtime: Ack. We'll add metric + last-chunk capture (obfuscated) and implement a 2s buffering grace for streaming tool-call args before throwing schema errors. We'll also prototype a sentinel approach.


 alex: Thanks — forwarding suggested mitigations to the customer and asking them to run the ALB tcpdump. Will update once we get capture.
